Log-Tail Derivatives by Quadrature of the Log-Density Derivatives

Source: R/log_tail.R
quad_log_tail_derivs.Rd

Computes the derivatives of order o of \(\log P\), where \(P\) is the tail beyond q on the side that lower.tail selects, from $$\log P = \ell(q) + \log J, \qquad J = \int_{\mathrm{tail}} e^{D(y)}\,dy, \qquad D(y) = \ell(y) - \ell(q).$$ The derivatives of \(\log J\) follow from the ratios \(\partial^B J / J\), which are weighted means of the complete Bell polynomials in the partial derivatives of \(D\), through the moment-to-cumulant sum; both sums are the recursions over the subsets of a multi-index that contain its first position, run in compiled code (log_tail_cumulants_cpp()) on the pairs that log_tail_pairs() enumerates. Every partial of \(D\) is a difference of the family's own log-density derivatives at \(y\) and at \(q\), which stays small over the tail, so the sums carry no cancellation of the size that the ratios of cdf_scale_k() carry, and the computation does not underflow where \(P\) does.

Usage

quad_log_tail_derivs(distrib, q, theta, o, lower.tail, all_orders = FALSE)

quad_log_tail_prob(distrib, q, theta, lower.tail)

Arguments

distrib

A continuous distribution object.

q

A numeric vector of quantiles inside the support.

theta

A named list of parameters; each has the length of q.

o

The derivative order, 1 to 4.

lower.tail

A single logical; TRUE selects the lower tail and FALSE the upper tail.

all_orders

Return the orders 1 to o, as a list of such lists?

Value

A named list, one component per multi-index of order o, in the order of deriv_names(), with the attribute "lost".

quad_log_tail_prob() returns \(\log P = \ell(q) + \log J\), a numeric vector of the length of q.

Details

The integral is taken with the 15-point Kronrod rule on 16 panels in \(u \in [0, 128]\). With \(s = 1/|\partial_y \ell(q)|\) the scale on which \(\ell\) falls away from \(q\), the map is \(y = q \pm s\,(e^{u} - 1)\) toward an infinite end of the support, which turns an exponential tail into a double exponential and a polynomial one into an exponential in \(u\), and \(y = b + (q - b)\exp\{-c\,(e^{u} - 1)\}\), \(c = \min(1, s/|q - b|)\), toward a finite end \(b\), which reaches \(b\) at \(u = \infty\) and turns a power of \(y - b\) into a double exponential. The route is meant for the far tail, where the density decreases away from q; log_tail_route() uses it below \(\log P = -5\). Toward an end at zero, a row whose last node with a representable abscissa still carries a relative weight above \(10^{-12}\), while the nodes beyond it have underflowed to zero, has mass below the smallest double (a shape near zero); it is marked in the attribute "lost" of the result. Toward an infinite end the nodes past the largest double are dropped, which leaves out a relative mass of order \((q/x_{\max})^{\nu}\) for a polynomial tail of index \(\nu\).

quad_tail_parts() returns the nodes at every quantile, the response vector \((q, y_1, \dots)\), in which the parameters are repeated to match, the log densities and the weights \(e^{D}\) times the Jacobian and the rule's weight; log_tail_nodes() the nodes and weights in \(u\), computed once; log_tail_pairs() the components of orders 1 to o in canonical form and, for each, the pairs (subset containing the first position, rest) as indices into the components.

Examples

d <- gamma1_distrib()
# This is log S of a gamma at 3000, where S underflows.
distributions7:::quad_log_tail_derivs(d, 3000, list(mu = 1.7, phi = 2.3),
                                      1L, lower.tail = FALSE)
#> $mu
#> [1] 451.6635
#> 
#> $phi
#> [1] 332.1425
#> 
#> attr(,"lost")
#> [1] FALSE
